title: GitBook Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Limits
summary: GitBook pricing includes three plans: Free for individuals, Essential ($65/site/month), and Ultimate ($249/site/month). Paid plans require upfront payment.
body_markdown:
## Automating GitBook Chores With Activepieces


It won't lower your GitBook bill, but Activepieces can take over the manual chores around GitBook so your editors spend their seats on writing instead of relaying messages.


Its free plan covers up to 5 users, with 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows, which matches the five-person team priced above.


Defined plainly, a flow's a workflow: a trigger followed by one or more actions. An integration's a connector to another app, such as Slack or Stripe.


If your team has no repetitive hand-offs around its docs, skip it; it adds a tool to maintain and saves you nothing.


Below, the screenshot shows the shape of a flow. A Stripe "Payment Failed" trigger feeds a Slack "Send Message To A Channel" action, and the run details on the left mark the step completed with a "Run succeeded" notice.


This one is about billing, not docs, but the pattern's the point: one event in one app, one message in another, with no person in between. Any chore you currently do by copy-pasting between tabs fits that pattern.


Two docs chores follow that same pattern.


### Announce published docs changes


When someone publishes a change, the people who depend on the docs, such as support and sales, often learn about it by accident.


A flow can watch for the change and post a short message to a team channel in Slack, so the announcement happens every time instead of whenever someone remembers.


What this chore costs is attention, not money, and that's where the saving lies.


Once readers leave feedback, it goes stale in whichever inbox catches it first. A flow can take each submission and send it to the channel or tracker where the owning team already works.


Nobody has to triage by hand, and the editor seats you pay for stay on writing rather than sorting.
